content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I set up a test website using the [product_name] Web Editor. My issue is that when I use the red switch to change the V1.0 variable to "1", the visualization should show a motor icon. When V1.0 goes back to "0" through the NI1 -- NQ1 input/output, the display should change to a red disk. Although V1.0 activates properly, this change doesn't show up on the website. I even added a delay to keep the status at "1" for a while, assuming it could be a data transmission lag, but it didn’t help. Does anyone have suggestions?

Please upload your test files for [product_name] Web Editor and [product_name] Soft Comfort. Sometimes picture formats can be unreliable. However, based on your timer circuit, it won't function as you intended.
I've simplified the website so that only the button remains. While the program operates correctly, I still don't see image changes as expected.

You may have noticed that the output Q1 only stays on for the set time of 2 seconds. Since I'm not clear about your overall goal, I'm just following your approach so far. Try using the circuit I've attached.

Thank you! It's true, Q1 in my program is just for testing. My aim is to get the pushbutton to work, but [product_name] Web Editor doesn't update the image when you press the button—image changes corresponding to states "1" or "0" aren’t reflected. I added a 2-second delay to the "1" state thinking it might solve delays in communication between the PLC and the website.
Has my suggestion solved your problem? If so, please mark the topic as resolved.
Thank you. It might not be possible for the variable 1.0 to update visually on the website between its "1" and "0" states. Apologies. How do I indicate that the topic is resolved?
I'm still not sure what your actual issue is, based on your last comment. Could you clarify what exactly you are trying to achieve?

Using [product_name] Web Editor, we've created a website to use certain controls. However, the tool only offers switches—not push buttons. The switch status is shown by displaying a GIF or JPG based on whether its associated variable is 1 or 0. What I wanted to do is reflect the real-time state (1 or 0) of the variable in the web interface acting as a pushbutton, but so far I've only managed to display a static image for either state 0 or state 1. Even though V1.0 changes state, the website doesn’t update the button’s image accordingly.

If I understand correctly, you're trying to animate a 'push button' on your web server so that pressing it visually changes the image. You’re using the Q1 output to check the button’s effect. To mark the topic as resolved: On the left above your first post, there's an 'Actions' button. Click it and a pop-up window will open (see attached image).

Yes, that was my goal—to activate a button on the website to change V1.0 to 1, read the input on NI1, then set V1.0 back to 0 through NQ1, and test if this change could be visualized on the website. It seems this isn't currently possible. Thanks for your help.
If there’s a workaround, please let me know. I’ll mark the topic solved. Thanks again for all your support.

With my previous suggestion, it’s possible. The network input feeds into a positive edge evaluator—this evaluator stays active for only one cycle at signal 1 and triggers a 2-second delay before switching off. The delay keeps the network output at 1 for 2 seconds. This causes V1.0 to hold the 1-state for 2 seconds.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are finding that changes in variable states within the backend logic do not result in timely updates to visual elements on websites built with [product_name] Web Editor. This leads to confusion and limits reliability for real-time feedback. Additionally, the absence of genuine pushbutton controls restricts the fidelity of the interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] Web Editor to provide real-time visual updates for variable state changes and support true pushbutton behaviors, not just switch-based controls.
